title: Dynamic reranker orchestration and regression watchtower
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a dynamic reranker orchestration layer that selects cross-encoder variants per-request (locale, query length, latency budget) and integrates an automated regression watchtower for staged rollouts. The goal is to reduce p99 tail latency for rerank endpoints while preserving or improving ranking quality across supported locales. This ticket implements model selection logic, runtime policy hooks, canary gating, and ties into the existing regression harness and perf dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Per-request selection policy chooses an appropriate cross-encoder variant and logs selection metadata to tracing (model_id, reason, predicted latency)
AC2: Canary rollout mechanism can route 1%, 5%, 20% traffic buckets to new variants and automatically pause at a regression threshold
AC3: Regression watchtower triggers alerts when quality drop > 0.5% on owned eval set or latency p99 increases > 15% in canary window
AC4: Fallback path exists (lightweight locale-aware candidate rescoring) if selected variant exceeds runtime error or latency budget
AC5: Dashboard shows per-variant quality metrics by locale, token-length bucket, and cost-per-kept-result
success_metrics: Metric: Reduce rerank p99 latency by 12% across high-traffic locales
Metric: Maintain or improve normalized ranking score on eval set (delta >= 0)
Metric: Keep canary-induced customer-impact events < 0.1% over 30 days
Metric: CPU/GPU cost per 1k requests decreases by 8% for mixed workloads
design_decisions: Decision: Use a lightweight rule-based first-pass to map request attributes (locale, length, latency_budget) to a candidate model family before consulting runtime telemetry
Decision: Implement soft-decision scoring (confidence) so we can fall back to hybrid rescoring when confidence is low
Decision: Store selection policies in config so product can tune weights without deploys (feature-flagged)
Decision: Canary windows will be tied to our regression harness outputs and require both quality and latency checks to pass before widening
implementation_tasks: Task 1: Add request attribute enrichment (locale detection, tokenized length estimate) to rerank API handler
Task 2: Implement policy engine that returns model_id and expected_latency; persist selection metadata to trace/log
Task 3: Integrate selection logic into the serving runtime path with minimal overhead (inline C++ hot path changes and Python control plane config)
Task 4: Wire canary gating with rollout controller and implement automatic pause/revert on regression signals
Task 5: Extend regression harness to evaluate selected variant on per-locale eval sets and report to watchtower
Task 6: Add dashboard panels for per-variant p50/p95/p99, quality delta, and cost-per-request
Task 7: Create migration plan and data retention for historical selection telemetry
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Spike complete — measured 18% worse latency when naively running heavy cross-encoders on short queries; validated need for selection policy (Maya).
2026-01-25: Policy prototype implemented in control plane; returns model_id with expected_latency estimate. Microbenchmark shows <1ms added overhead (Arjun).
2026-01-28: Canary controller stubbed; integrated with feature flags. First canary run against internal traffic started — baseline collection only (Lucia).
2026-02-02: Regression watchtower integration complete; hook subscribed to rerank evaluation job. Initial thresholds set conservatively to avoid false positives (Maya).
review_feedback: PM (Priya Rao): Ensure we expose a simple override in Console for emergency switches and for customer-specific model pinning.
Design (Ethan Park): Add UI affordance in Console to visualize locale-level performance and allow filtering by token-length buckets.
SRE (Nina Gomez): Add circuit-breaker behavior if a variant exceeds 2x predicted latency to protect downstream services.
Security (Rahul Mehta): Confirm that selection telemetry does not leak PII; strip raw text from logs and only persist hashes.
